title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
A self-driving car in autonomous mode struck and killed a duck in a residential neighborhood in Austin, Texas, while a human safety operator was present in the vehicle. The vehicle did not slow down or stop before hitting the duck. The failure occurred in the perception or decision-making layer of the system, which did not recognize a small animal as an obstacle requiring avoidance.

A human safety operator was in the vehicle but did not intervene. It is not established whether the operator had time to react, whether the system's behavior fell within acceptable parameters for the deployment, or what conditions would have made such an intervention possible. The company stated it found no evidence of a separate claimed failure at a stop sign.

The incident would have required either better trained animal detection in the autonomous system before deployment, or override protocols that gave the human operator sufficient warning and control to prevent the collision. Whether the system was designed or tested for detecting and avoiding small animals in its operating domain is not established.

reports.title: A self-driving car in Texas hit and killed a mother duck, sparking neighborhood outrage
Residents say self-driving car killed duck in Mueller
Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood of Austin, Texas, prompting significant community backlash. The incident occurred when the self-driving car, which had a human safety operator present, ran over the duck without slowing down or stopping. The duck, which had been nesting in a pot outside a local Italian restaurant, was familiar to residents, intensifying their concerns about autonomous vehicle safety in their neighborhood.

Avride confirmed the vehicle was operating in autonomous mode during the incident and stated that it found no evidence supporting a resident's claim that the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign. The company has since restricted its testing operations by excluding certain streets around the lake and is now conducting simulated experiments to improve the technology's ability to avoid similar situations. Local residents have placed the duck's eggs in an incubator. Multiple autonomous vehicle companies, including Zoox, Tesla, and Waymo, currently test or operate services in Austin.
